title: side by side graphs
explanation:
### Description

This example displays two graphs side by side in split viewports within a single render window. The left viewport shows a triangle graph (three vertices, three edges) and the right shows a single-edge graph (two vertices, one edge), both using force-directed layouts with different background colors.

**dataset → input → layout → filter → visual_asset → renderer → infrastructure → output**

- [vtkForceDirectedLayoutStrategy](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkForceDirectedLayoutStrategy.html) computes vertex positions using force simulation.
- [vtkGraphLayout](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkGraphLayout.html) applies the layout strategy to each graph.
- [vtkGraphToPolyData](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkGraphToPolyData.html) converts graph edges to polydata lines.
- [vtkMutableUndirectedGraph](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkMutableUndirectedGraph.html) builds undirected graphs.
- [vtkPoints](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPoints.html) positions vertices explicitly.
- [vtkPolyDataMapper](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPolyDataMapper.html) maps edge polydata to graphics primitives.
- [vtkRenderer](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderer.html) provides split viewports for side-by-side display.
